Hi Helen — thanks for the list. Posting a quick summary below and looping in Neha (SRE) to confirm the operational details and share logs/diagrams. Marcus from account is on cc to track next steps around an SLA exception if you need a longer hold.

Short answers up-front:
- Deletion propagation: deletions are replicated as "tombstones" to geo-copies within the normal replication window (typically <6 hours for your profile), but permanent expunge is handled by a background expunger that runs on a configurable cadence (default 30 days after tombstone).
- Expunge vs tombstone: tombstones mark objects as deleted and prevent new restores; expunge permanently removes low-level blocks and metadata. Expunge is what reduces backup size across copies.
- Forensic restores: we support point-in-time restores from any geo-copy until the expunge completes. After expunge, only metadata snapshots (if retained via a legal hold) can be used — otherwise the data is unrecoverable.

Pending items for Neha: exact replication SLO for your account, how legal hold requests are enacted (ticket + retention flag or short-term SLA), and the list of artifacts we can provide for audits (replication logs, tombstone timelines, restore receipts).

Neha — can you confirm and attach the flow diagram + a recent replication-lag sample? Also flag if we need an official exception process documented for Greenshore.

Hi all — attaching the high-level diagram and a small sample of replication lag metrics. Key details below (operational):

1) Replication & visibility
- Primary delete -> tombstone generation: immediate (at commit).
- Tombstone replication: streamed to geo-copies; typical 99th percentile is ~3.5 hours for accounts with reserved throughput (Greenshore profile), worst-case bursts up to 12 hours. See attached replication-lag-sample.csv for a 30-day histogram.

2) Expunge lifecycle
- Expunge job: background job that compacts and purges tombstoned objects from storage blobs. Default schedule: once every 24 hours; object-level TTL = 30 days from tombstone by default.
- Expunge propagation: once an object is expunged in the primary, expunge jobs on the geo-copy will detect tombstone markers and perform local block expunge in the next scheduled run (within 24 hours). That means permanent removal from offsite typically occurs within 31 days (30d TTL + local expunge cycle), but actual timing depends on backlog and replication lag.

3) Legal hold / audit holds
- We support a retention hold flag that overrides expunge for specified object paths/ids. To place a hold we require: ticket (support+legal), endpoint, and hold duration. We can do temporary holds (30/60/90 days) or indefinite holds for audit — long holds require an agreement and may incur storage/operational fees.

4) Forensic restore & evidence
- Until expunge completion, we can perform point-in-time restores from geo-copies. For audits we can provide: tombstone timelines, replication delivery receipts (per-chunk), and a restore receipt showing the exact snapshot and manifest used.

Attachments: backup-flow-diagram.pdf (flow + expunge timeline), replication-lag-sample.csv (30-day window).

- Greenshore: confirm whether you need an extended hold for the upcoming compliance review and requested duration.
- Redwood: if hold requested, Marcus to submit an exception/contract addendum; SRE will log hold flags and confirm impacts.

Let me know if you want a short runbook we can attach to your audit pack.
